content.text:
I've submitted index 9 (Sb fraction 0.349) as the best composition. It had the highest measured EQE, 0.125%, and index 10 next to it (Sb 0.375) was nearly the same at 0.122%. I don't know where the true peak on the line is, because the gaps between measured points are large.

I used all 5 EQE measurements and 3 of the 5 XRD measurements.

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | 0.219 | 0.021 |
| **9** | **0.349** | **0.125** |
| 10 | 0.375 | 0.122 |
| 19 | 0.661 | 0.0086 |
| 26 | 0.819 | 0.0046 |

- **Where the best region is:** EQE is highest around Sb 0.35–0.38 and falls off sharply on both sides. The composition I first expected to be good, index 19 (the ideal NiSb₂O₆ ratio of 0.667), performed poorly.
- **Why XRD didn't settle it:** samples at Sb 0.29, 0.35 and 0.45 gave the same diffraction pattern. They share one crystal structure, so the XRD scans couldn't show which of them would perform best.
- **What's still open:** indices 8 (Sb 0.32) and 11 (Sb 0.41) were never measured and could beat index 9. With the last measurement I checked index 10, just past index 9, because it seemed the most likely to do well.
